lines.en: What’s it like to be “special?”
You always told me that’s what I was but, in my eyes, you were the one who fit that bill the best.
I was just me. And you were just you. But you were the first one I loved. So that must count for something, right?
I wonder what you’d say if you could see me now.
I wonder if you’d still call me special.
Or if I’ve become so forgettable that you’d take one look at me before turning around and purging me from your memory.
There might be other forces at play when it comes to that outcome, sure. I mean, just look at where we are.
Saying this city is a place that’s grounded in reality would be a bit of a stretch, wouldn’t it? Especially when there are ten or twelve things each day proving the exact opposite.
But that’s just the problem. This place IS grounded in reality. It’s all of US that make it seem so weird. It’s what WE see — what WE feel.
And you feel more than anyone.
I remember the sound of your heartbeat — how irregular it was. But also how comfortable and calm it made me feel when I’d lie there on your chest.
You felt like an earthquake back then.
But I was just me. And you were just you.
And that’s all we ever needed to be, since our home was far more fortunate than the one you find yourself in now.
But, hey...
I hope you’re having fun.
I know you’re not, but I hope you are.
And that’s probably silly of me. But that’s the way I’ve always been.
Your precious little trickster.
Your kick to the shin.
Your lifejacket.
: What the fuck is this place?
: A home away from home.
: And it’s yours?
: How long have you had this and why haven’t you told me about it yet? An extra apartment is the solution to like nine-hundred of our problems.
: You must have me confused with someone else. I don’t have any problems with you.
: This is our very first meeting. And the only reason I’ve taken you here is because I’m a bad person.
: Sorry, are we roleplaying now? Who am I supposed to be this time?
: Someone better at hiding their feelings.
: Ughhhh. Ayane again?
: Do you want something to drink?
: Oooh, I get a beverage this time? How nice. You weren’t abducted by aliens as well, were you?
: Do you want something or not?
: Coffee, please.
: I have a feeling I’ll need the energy.
: Are you sure you don’t want me to be your partner? Because I swear I’m really good at this game. I’m not just lying about being good at it for clout like Imani.
: Bitch, I ain’t lyin’ ‘bout shit. Sit yo ass down.
: I am quite positive, Rika. Especially due to the fact that this is a one-on-one competition between Imani and me to decide the winner of the Dorm Wars.
: So like, how’s that shit work exactly? Ain’t the first floor still up by one after we got the point for that weird fuckin’ leg game?

: Technically, yes. But, given that Maya’s been absent for the entire competition and very likely won’t show up in the final hour, you guys are getting one point docked. Which makes the score four to four.
: Which, if you have learned anything about math, would indicate that this is a “winner takes all” scenario.
: I know how fuckin’ numbers work, goth lady.
: Congratulations, Yamaguchi. You have detention on Friday as well now.
: Now, I’m not trying to overstep my boundaries or whatever, but I’m pretty sure you can’t give my students detention for things they do outside of school hours.
: Cause, if that were the case, we’d all have detention right now for hanging out at a strip club.
: My spotless school record is suddenly in danger. I must leave this place at once.
: “Spotless” my ass — you’ve got a D in biology.
: I will never understand the purpose of gonads no matter how many times it is explained to me.
: Imani, just throw the fucking ball already.
: Bitch, let me aim!
: Rin! After Wakana and Imani are done playing beer pong, do you and your friends want to play?! Because I do! And I don’t have other friends so I need to borrow yours!
: Please don’t get your daughter drunk in the presence of school teachers, Rika.
: I’m 42, Wakana. I can do whatever I want.
: You certainly can n-
: Ha!
: Fuck yeah!
: Oh, nice job. But why was the splash sound so violently realistic?
: That’s just how I roll, girl. Beat that, Wakana.
: That was luck and you know it. We’ve played this game at least twenty times at the bar and not once have you sunk anything on your first shot.
: Yeah, but I’ve never had the fate of the second floor in my hands before. I am being empowered by my responsibility and love for ten very strange girls! Several of whom are currently absent.
: Ain’t you supposed to be responsible for all of us as our teacher and shit? Not just the second floor?
: The rest of you are my responsibility for now. Then, after tonight, I can go back to not caring about anything that happens to any of you who aren’t named Miyamura.
: Huh? What? I heard my name.
: Miyamura- retrieve that ball from that cup. I’d do it myself, but I’m too old and frail and would likely hurt myself in the process.
: Wakana, you’re more than capable of getting it yourself. You can’t blame everything on your back and shouldn’t be making Makoto do your bidding.
: Old? Aren’t you in your 20’s?
: Yes. But you’ll soon find that means nothing in the face of aging’s terrible effects on the human body. Then, next thing you know, you won’t even have the motivation to go to the gym anymore.
: Speak for yourself. I still go every day.
: I’ve never even set foot in a gym. But sure, I’ll get your ball if it brings us closer to winning the competition.
: Disqualification! Makoto touched the ball! This means Wakana’s enlisted a partner and has broken the rules of one-on-one beer pong!
: As official referee, I declare that no rules have been broken and that anyone can touch any balls they want!
: What wonderful news, Osako. I’ve gotten the green light from Rika as well. I’m just one Tinder profile away from heterosexuality now, aren’t I?
: Not now, Wakana...not here.
: I’m glad everyone seems to be having fun again. Between Yasu collapsing and the end of the Newly-Newlywed Game, things got pretty intense for a little, didn’t they?
: Yes, but...at least we wound up winning the...leg thing. A second tragic loss might make me believe we’re not really as close as we think.
: What do you mean? Of course we are! No silly competition could ever get in the way of our friendship.
: You...really think we’re that indestructible?
: Do you not? Is my undying love for you unrequited?
: No, I just...mean there’s gotta be something that could cause a rift in our friendship, right?
: Just look at Miss Watabe and her girlfriend. If even they’re fighting right now, there’s probably no relationship strong enough to survive everything...right?
: You think they’re fighting?
: Is that...not what all of the tension we’ve been seeing ever since she showed up means?...
: The tension seems pretty one-sided, I think. Maybe they’re just horny?
: Yeah...maybe.
: Is everything okay, Sana? You’ve seemed kind of weird for a little while now.
: Do you think...
: Just...out of curiosity...do you think that stuff Nodoka said about Io had any truth to it?...
: That she was...you know...
: Hah...
: I don’t know, but...I hope not.
: I’m trying to forget about it since it feels like a complete invasion of privacy, but...it would definitely explain some things.
: And Nodoka was right about all of that other stuff, so...
: Nodoka’s...kind of a really bad person if she’d just...say that in front of everybody, isn’t she?...
: Yeah...
: It really makes you wonder if there was more to that stuff with Yumi in the classroom from a while ago.
: Like, what if she really did do something to provoke her and just...none of us knew about it?
: It’s not really...like we can ask Yumi either since none of us talk to her.
: I think she just wants to be left alone for the most part. But hey, she’s been fitting in a little better lately and...that’s good, I guess.
: Yeah...fitting in is...hard enough as is...
: You’ve been doing well, though. But despite your sudden up-tick in conversations with others, I think the thing I’m most excited about is the fact that I get to see both of your eyes every day now.
: Are you...flirting with me?
: I can think you’re cute without flirting, you know. You’re like a doll.
: And besides, I like boys. One boy, to be specific. Well...one man. But you get the point.
: Yeah...I get the point.
: How about you, though?
: What do you mean?
: Well, my child — without beating around the bush, I’ve been noticing some changes in you lately. And you are at the age now, so I don’t hold it against you.
: But I don’t think I’ve ever really asked you how you felt about girls on a...sexual level.
: You don’t have to tell me if you don’t want to. But you should know that my opinion of you won’t change no matter how you answer.
: I don’t...
: I don’t really...know how I feel, but...
: I think...
: I think I do...like them like that...
: But I like boys too.
: Then you’ll fit right in with the rest of the class. Like half of us are bi at this point. And hey, that gives you a bunch of options as well.
: Ayane...
: Is there anyone in particular who catches your eye? Anyone who interests you?
: Ayane...there’s...I...
: Maybe Rin? You two have kissed already.
: Did you like it? How did it make you feel?
: Ayane, I like Sensei.
: Like...a lot.
: I’m sorry I didn’t tell you sooner. I just...
: You’ve liked him for so long and...
: I didn’t want this to happen.
: I tried so hard to avoid it...for so long...but he just...
: He kept coming...
: He kept looking at me...
: And somewhere along the line, I stopped wanting to get away and...
: And wanting to be with him instead.
: Ayane, I’m really sorry.
: Why are you apologizing? I’ve known this even longer than you have.
: Because...because I wasn’t...I wasn’t supposed to get in the way. I don’t want to get in the way. Of your happiness, I mean.
: Sana, you’re not my only friend with a crush on the same man as me. And, as I’m sure you’ve noticed, pretty much every single girl in our class feels the same way as you. This changes nothing.
: But it might.
: It won’t.
: But...I’m not going to hold back, you know.
: I wouldn’t expect you to. Nothing’s ever easy when it comes to love.
: You can do whatever you want. I’m still going to win in the end.
: You sound...pretty confident about that.
: I’ve told you before — confidence is what makes a girl attractive.
: But I’m sure I don’t need to tell you what it is that makes a girl attractive now that you’re finally figuring out who you are.
: I’m really proud of you, Sana.
: You’ve come such a long way.
: And to think that, to you...it’s probably only been a few months.
: Ayane...
: Whatever happens, I want you to follow your heart.
: I’ll love you no matter what.
: There’s...
: There’s something else I should tell you too...
: Both sides have one cup remaining! The next person to sink a shot wins!
: Yes. Thank you, referee. I have never played this game before and do not have eyes, so there is no way I could have possibly known any of that.
: Think for a second, Wakana. Do you really want to make this shot?
: Because we’ve got several transfers from your class on the second floor. And me winning means they win. Which is kind of like you winning in a way, right?
: Do you know what else is also like “me winning?” Me. Winning.
: Fly!
: Oh, fuck yeah!
: Prepare to meet your manufacturer.
: Shit!
: So close, yet so far! Could this be the most exciting, nail-biting event in sports history?! I think so, folks!
: Death ball was literally like three hours ago.
: Any last words, Wakana?
: Yes. Please miss.
: Never!
: Tch!
: Welp.
: FLOOR TWOOOOO! LET’S FUCKING GOOOOOO!
: Double or nothing!
: Double what? Cause we ain’t playin’ for cash and losing the point I just got would mean the first floor takes the whole ass competition.
: Then we’ll play for cash.
: Osako, my purse.
: I want in this time! Rin! Let’s take everything Wakana’s got and force her and Osako out onto the street!
: Bruh, we ain’t got that much time left. We’ve gotta start cleaning this place up or the strippers will realize we threw a party here.
: They don’t know we’re here?!
: Hell nah! You really think they’d rent this place out for a high school party? There ain’t nothin’ legal about this.
: Rin! Change of plans! Get the car! We’ve gotta bail! I can’t afford to get arrested again!
: What car?!
: Yours!
: I don’t have a- wait, did you steal my neighbor’s car?!
